svg.title: Three ways to compose the organ with a model: as a library around any model, behind a frozen prompt around an open model, and in the decode loop of a model trained with it
svg.desc: Three panels, the organ drawn identically at the bottom of each: a journal sealed per scope, a gate on the write, an index on the read, a lifecycle; a cue goes in, a window of retrieved lines comes out and rises to the model, and the model's answer, cite a label and give the attribute or abstain, goes to a harness that maps the label to the pointer and verifies it. Panel one, the organ as a library: any model of any size behind any runtime, the window as text in the integrator's prompt, the cue from the integrator's encoder or the hash seeded address, no training; it inherits the organ's guarantees by design and the organ level rows, and the pair is to be measured with the protocol. Panel two, a model people use: an open model with frozen weights at a pinned revision, the window as text in a frame whose hash is in the record, the organ's hash seeded cue, no training; first execution retained and not graved, the episodic conditions hold and the skill arm fails at the size run. Panel three, the cortex trained with the organ: the window as content through a zero initialised cross attention gated by the router, a cue encoder learned by contrast, one fine tune; the model alone INVALID at this size, the system PASS on the live seeds under the organ side policy. No measured number appears in the figure.
